name: Nuclear risk
value: No US–Russia treaty limits since Feb
summary: NATO reportedly believes Russia is ready to launch a nuclear-armed satellite; no US–Russia arms-control treaty in force
state: German media reported on 23 Nov that NATO intelligence believes Russia is ready to launch a nuclear-armed satellite (Reuters); Russia has not confirmed this. No US–Russia treaty limits have applied since New START lapsed, and the White House has renewed its call for trilateral arms-control talks with Russia and China (Arms Control Association). No nuclear test, alert-level change or threatened use in an active conflict was found to 23 Nov, so Watch holds on the arms-control lapse.
for_you: No change in official UK public guidance. The risk here is long-term erosion of arms-control limits rather than an immediate threat.
rubric_hit: Arms-control lapse without replacement = Watch; no test, alert change or threatened use

sources.title: Reuters — NATO believes Russia is ready to launch nuclear-armed satellite, German media say
Arms Control Association — White House renews call for trilateral arms control talks

why: Nuclear use anywhere would be a civilisational shock; arms-control treaties are weaker than at any time since the 1960s.
drivers: Threats in active wars, testing, doctrine changes, arms-control collapse, proliferation.

rubric.alert: A nuclear test, changes in deployment/alert levels, or threatened use in an active conflict.
rubric.watch: Explicit threats, unusual exercises, doctrine changes, or arms-control lapses without replacement.
rubric.normal: No explicit nuclear threats or tests; arms-control dialogue active.
